title: Archaeopteryx
summary: Archaeopteryx was an early feathered, bird-like animal that lived around 150 million years ago in the Late Jurassic, in the lagoon deposits of the Solnhofen area of Bavaria. Its first fossil, a feather, turned up in 1861, and all 12 known specimens come from that area.

uncertainty.note: Sources say 'around' or 'about' 150 million years; no error range given.

where.modern_name: Solnhofen-Eichstätt area, Altmühltal Nature Park, Bavaria, Germany
where.historical_name: Solnhofen-Eichstätt lagoon area (Late Jurassic); not a polity

paleo.not_applicable: Plate-model reconstructions of this point at 150 Ma disagree widely (three models gave very different positions); none adopted.

importance.justification: Iconic early bird whose fossils were debated in the 1860s evolution dispute.

sources.title: An 150-Million-Year-Old Fossil Is the Link Between Birds and Dinosaurs
sources.publisher: Natural History Museum of Utah, University of Utah

reviewer_note: Pin is the IUGS serial-site coordinate (48°53'25"N, 10°58'05"E), a proxy for the Solnhofen-Eichstätt area, not a single find spot. 150 Ma is approximate. Sources differ on whether the 1861 find was a feather or skeleton.
